--- title: "GiBleed — Exercises (Solutions)" subtitle: "Worked answers with real federated output" format: html: df-print: kable execute: warning: false message: false error: true --- Download the solutions (.R) Back to the exercises ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DSI); library(DSOpal); library(dsBaseClient); library(dsOMOPClient) builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder() builder$append(server = "nairobi", url = "https://nairobi.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") builder$append(server = "douala", url = "https://douala.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") builder$append(server = "dakar", url = "https://dakar.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") conns <- DSI::datashield.login(logins = builder$build()) ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop_demo.gibleed", symbol = "omop", conns = conns) or_table <- function(fit) { co <- fit$coefficients data.frame(term = rownames(co), OR = round(co[, "P_OR"], 3), CI_low = round(co[, "low0.95CI.P_OR"], 3), CI_high = round(co[, "high0.95CI.P_OR"], 3), p_value = signif(co[, "p-value"], 3), row.names = NULL) } ``` ::: # Exercise 1 — Explore the medications ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ds.omop.concept.prevalence("drug_exposure", metric = "persons", top_n = 12, scope = "pooled", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| concept_id| n_persons|concept_name | |----------:|---------:|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 40213227| 2655|tetanus and diphtheria toxoids, adsorbed, preservative free, for adult use | | 1127433| 2575|Acetaminophen 325 MG Oral Tablet | | 40213160| 2135|poliovirus vaccine, inactivated | | 1713671| 2015|Amoxicillin 250 MG / Clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet | | 19059056| 1920|Aspirin 81 MG Oral Tablet | | 1118084| 1840|celecoxib | | 40213296| 1730|hepatitis A vaccine, adult dosage | | 40213306| 1555|hepatitis B vaccine, adult dosage | | 1127078| 1425|Acetaminophen 160 MG Oral Tablet | | 40229134| 1385|Acetaminophen 21.7 MG/ML / Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide 1 MG/ML / doxylamine succinate 0.417 MG/ML Oral Solution | | 19078461| 1270|Ibuprofen 200 MG Oral Tablet | | 19133873| 1270|Penicillin V Potassium 250 MG Oral Tablet |
::: ```{.r .cell-code} ds.omop.concept.lookup(1118084, symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| concept_id|concept_name |domain_id |vocabulary_id |standard_concept | |----------:|:------------|:---------|:-------------|:----------------| | 1118084|celecoxib |Drug |RxNorm |S |
::: ::: > **Answer.** Celecoxib (`1118084`) is taken by **~1,840** patients — one of the most common drugs in this NSAID-heavy synthetic cohort. # Exercise 2 — Build a boolean table ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age", year = 2019), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 192671, format = "binary", name = "gi_bleed"), omop_variable(table = "drug_exposure", concept_id = 1118084, format = "binary", name = "celecoxib") ), output = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec, out = c(study = "M"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ds.colnames("M", datasources = conns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> $nairobi #> [1] "person_id" "gi_bleed" "celecoxib" "sex" "age" #> #> $douala #> [1] "person_id" "gi_bleed" "celecoxib" "sex" "age" #> #> $dakar #> [1] "person_id" "gi_bleed" "celecoxib" "sex" "age" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ds.dim("M", datasources = conns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> $`dimensions of M in nairobi` #> [1] 889 5 #> #> $`dimensions of M in douala` #> [1] 878 5 #> #> $`dimensions of M in dakar` #> [1] 927 5 #> #> $`dimensions of M in combined studies` #> [1] 2694 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} as.data.frame(ds.table("M$celecoxib", datasources = conns)$output.list[["TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts"]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> #> Data in all studies were valid #> #> Study 1 : No errors reported from this study #> Study 2 : No errors reported from this study #> Study 3 : No errors reported from this study ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display}
| | ds.table("M$celecoxib", datasources = conns)$output.list[["TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts"]]| |:--|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:| |0 | 850| |1 | 1844| |NA | 0|
::: ::: > **Answer.** `M` has one row per patient (~2,700 combined) with `person_id, sex, age, gi_bleed, celecoxib`. Both clinical columns are `binary` (0/1 presence); the server built exactly the table the recipe described. # Exercise 3 — Is celecoxib associated with GI bleeding? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- ds.glm(formula = "M$gi_bleed ~ M$age + M$sex + M$celecoxib", family = "binomial", datasources = conns) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} or_table(fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|term | OR| CI_low| CI_high| p_value| |:-----------|-----:|------:|-------:|-------:| |(Intercept) | 0.132| 0.090| 0.190| 0.00000| |M$age | 1.002| 0.996| 1.008| 0.57200| |M$sexM | 1.018| 0.835| 1.241| 0.86000| |M$celecoxib | 1.397| 1.118| 1.746| 0.00327|
::: ::: > **Answer.** **Celecoxib is a significant predictor** — its odds ratio is **above 1** (≈ 1.4, p ≈ 0.003): patients on this NSAID have higher odds of a GI bleed, which is clinically sensible. Age and sex are not significant. (This is a *different* signal from the tutorial's peptic-ulcer model — a drug exposure rather than a prior condition.) # Exercise 4 — A different outcome: does age predict a fracture? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec_fx <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age", year = 2019), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 4278672, format = "binary", name = "fx_forearm") ), output = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec_fx, out = c(study = "FX"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) fit_fx <- ds.glm(formula = "FX$fx_forearm ~ FX$age + FX$sex", family = "binomial", datasources = conns) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} or_table(fit_fx) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|term | OR| CI_low| CI_high| p_value| |:-----------|-----:|------:|-------:|-------:| |(Intercept) | 0.064| 0.044| 0.091| 0.000| |FX$age | 1.020| 1.014| 1.025| 0.000| |FX$sexM | 1.033| 0.851| 1.255| 0.741|
::: ::: > **Answer.** Now **age** is the significant predictor (OR slightly above 1 per year — older patients fracture more), while sex is not. The contrast with Exercise 3 is the lesson: *which* predictor matters depends on the outcome — a comorbidity drove GI bleeding, age drives fractures. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DSI::datashield.logout(conns) ``` :::
